key_insight: Turbulent temperature and humidity fluctuations strongly affect volatile-particle activation and subsequent ice-crystal growth, making turbulence essential to modeling early contrails from sustainable aviation fuels.
engineering_relevance: Contrail predictions for low-aromatic aviation fuels should resolve turbulent mixing and gas–aerosol coupling rather than rely solely on steady aerosol-jet models.
method: Large-eddy simulations coupled with a discretised population balance equation.
Experimental jet configuration reproducing upper-tropospheric thermodynamic conditions.
One-dimensional, one-way coupled population-balance modeling to assess activation pathways.
evidence_signal: Simulations captured jet-core cooling and bracketed experimental ice-crystal number concentration, mean diameter and mass density across selected values of unspecified parameters.
watch_item: Unspecified experimental parameters introduce uncertainty, and applicability to realistic engine configurations requires further study.
paper_title: The role of turbulent jet dynamics on contrail formation from conventional and sustainable aviation fuels
